lens_summaries.security: PASS — All WHERE predicates use SQLAlchemy parameterized ORM expressions (Column.in_(list), Column >= value); no raw SQL string interpolation. No secrets exposed. DS-013 compliance confirmed: place filter applied against InwardHeaderModel.place (denormalized snapshot), NOT against SupplierModel.place. The assert-based reconciliation check is an ADR-mandated pattern per DS-017 (is_adr_tradeoff: true) and mirrors the already-validated SalesReportService implementation. Note: assert is disabled by Python -O flag, but this is the DS-017 design intent (defense-in-depth for future refactors, not primary validation).

adr_tradeoffs_noted.note: assert consol_total == txn_total is disabled by Python -O flag. Accepted: DS-017 explicitly designates this as defense-in-depth for future refactors, not as a primary runtime invariant. Same pattern used in SalesReportService (previously validated CLEAN). No fix required.

positive_observations: Faithful DS-017 implementation: _build_filters() is the single WHERE source for both queries; _query_consolidation() and _query_transactions() accept only a pre-built filters list and add no inline predicates — enforces reconciliation by construction.
DS-013 compliance explicit: InwardHeaderModel.place used in both the place filter and the SELECT projection; SupplierModel joined only for supplier_name display. Docstring calls this out clearly.

Join root selection is correct: consolidation query roots from tbl_inward_line (design/grade aggregation); transactions query roots from tbl_inward_header (chronological per-line view). Both are semantically appropriate and match the SalesReportService mirror pattern.

Secondary sort InwardHeaderModel.header_id ASC on the transactions query provides deterministic ordering when multiple inward lines share the same purchase_date — correct extension beyond the minimum spec.
